author: Claude
headline: Dip picks hold steady after a Thanksgiving-shortened day; Altria eyes Imperial Brands
summary: US markets were shut for Thanksgiving, so the day's moves came mostly from London and Asia. Headlines focused on a large upward revision to US third-quarter GDP, new US tariffs and chip stocks, with Nvidia's volatile swings in the spotlight. The market backdrop still reads Cautious. The dip picks are led by AMD, TSMC, Freeport-McMoRan, Glencore, UnitedHealth and Dell, with Intel, Micron, Cisco, ASML, Arm and Netflix also well below their highs. Glencore rose 3.4% as miners kept bouncing, while Micron fell 4.5%. Dips can keep falling, so smaller buys spread the risk. Not financial advice.
points: US third-quarter GDP was revised sharply higher; Trump demanded a probe into the 'record setting error'.
Marlboro maker Altria is exploring a takeover of UK's Imperial Brands.
Chips: Micron -4.5%, ASML -2.5%, TSMC -2% today; Nvidia's volatile swings put risks of single-stock ETFs in focus.
Crypto: bitcoin's dormant supply is rising, a pattern seen in earlier bear-market bottoms, but every coin is still falling. Reckitt is flagged as a falling knife.
